notes: Re-checked at d8adcf18; both defects stand. (1) 95-99 and 214-218 print ExitFile and os.Exit(3) on any error, so a *LockTimeoutError from WithFileLock (lock.go:26-38) never reaches root.go:223-225 (exit 4 + lock hint). (2) 248-253: writeFoundPlan writes the task file (273) and queue (279) inside the store callback before foundrequest.go:169 writes the store; if that write fails, tasks exist but requests stay unapplied. openFoundOutcomes (founddedup.go:72-98) keys on stored state only and new ids avoid collisions (foundapply_test.go:131), so a retry opens a second found task.

resolved.evidence: Both defects fixed in internal/cli/found.go. (1) 87db2bd7: runFoundApply and runFoundAdd return a *LockTimeoutError instead of exit 3, so the root dispatcher exits 4 with the lock hint; TestFoundApplyAndAdd_LockContentionTimeoutExitsFour (b1b68b67) holds the task-file lock and the request-store lock for apply and the store lock for add, each red before the fix (exit 3, store-write hint) and green after. (2) 73188715: applyFoundRequests snapshots the task file and queue under the task-file lock and restores them (snapshotFoundFiles/restore, as tp found answer does) when the store write after writeFoundPlan fails; TestFoundApply_AFailedStoreWriteLeavesNoTaskBehind makes the store's directory read-only after its lock directory exists, was red before the fix (found-f1 left behind, retry opened found-f1-2, reproduced by hand too) and is green after: no task remains and the retry opens found-f1. Quality gate green: check-suite-state.sh, golangci-lint (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh, check-complexity.sh. Out of scope: in a project with no .git, LockFilePath for the store under .tp/ resolves to .tp/locks or .tp/.tp/locks depending on which directories exist, so add and apply can take different lock files for the same store; the tests apply once before holding the lock for that reason.
